rationale: The plan correctly identifies the 1-vs-1 design as inferentially void: it explicitly refuses DESeq()/nbinomWaldTest, computes size factors for normalization only, reports descriptive log2 fold changes with control set as the reference level, emits no p-values or adjusted p-values, and names the replicated design (n>=3 per group) that would restore inference — matching the reference. QC is design-appropriate (blind VST, PCA on top 500, sample distances, library sizes, with an explicit note that clustering/outlier inference is not meaningful at n=1), and the low-count filter (>=10 counts in >=1 sample, justified by smallest group size) and normalization-inside-DESeq2 handling are minimal and correct. The main weakness is the enrichment step: preranked fgsea on a fold-change ranking with no error model is not warranted here, and running it partly contradicts the plan's own no-p-value stance (the acceptance criteria even mention collapsing 'significant' sets while elsewhere disclaiming set-level p-values), though the universe, collection versions, rank metric, and 15-500 size window are all specified. Reporting is thorough, naming methods, versions, thresholds, gene counts before/after filtering, and the no-replication caveat up front in the executive summary.
